text.title: AI LLM Workload Architecture — Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 known failure modes of eval-driven LLM workload architectures. Each carries a detector (what to look for) and a repair (the corrective action).

failure-mode.description: Eval contamination: eval cases were copied into the few-shot block or the system prompt, so the metric measures memorisation, not quality.
failure-mode.detector: Grep the prompt files for any eval-case input string; any exact or near-exact hit. Also: eval score at or near 1.0 while production sampling shows failures.
failure-mode.repair: Move the leaked cases out of the prompt, regenerate the baseline run, and add a CI check that fails when an eval input appears in a prompt file.

failure-mode.description: Judge drift: the LLM judge runs on a floating model alias or with temperature above 0, so scores move with no code change.
failure-mode.detector: Two eval runs at the same commit differ by more than the stated tolerance; judge config shows an alias ("latest") or no pinned model id.
failure-mode.repair: Pin the judge model id and set temperature 0; record the judge prompt hash in the spec; re-run to establish the noise floor before trusting any threshold.

failure-mode.description: Vibes threshold: the "pass" criterion is a sentence ("responses feel better") rather than a number against a baseline run.
failure-mode.detector: Spec has no numeric threshold per metric, or has thresholds but `evidence[]` contains no baseline run URL.
failure-mode.repair: Run the current commit as the baseline, record its URL and per-metric scores, then set thresholds as baseline minus an explicit tolerance.

failure-mode.description: Silent model swap: production points at an alias, the vendor rotates the snapshot, and behaviour changes with no commit and no eval run.
failure-mode.detector: Runtime config or SDK call uses an alias or omits the version suffix; vendor changelog shows a snapshot change inside the window of a quality complaint.
failure-mode.repair: Pin the dated model id in config, add the id as a spec input, and route every model upgrade through the regression gate like a code change.

failure-mode.description: Gate bypassed: the prompt or retrieval config was edited in a path the CI filter does not watch (a YAML file, a database row, an f-string), so the eval suite never ran.
failure-mode.detector: Production prompt hash differs from the hash recorded at the last eval run; CI history shows no eval job for the deploying commit.
failure-mode.repair: Move prompts into version-controlled files under a watched path, compute and log the prompt hash at startup, and fail the deploy when it differs from the last gated hash.

failure-mode.description: No degradation path: a burst of 429 responses triggers unbounded retries or an unhandled exception, and the feature turns a throttle into an outage.
failure-mode.detector: No retry ceiling or backoff in the client code; no eval case exercises the timeout/429 branch; error dashboards show retry storms during vendor incidents.
failure-mode.repair: Add bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter, define the fallback (secondary pinned model, cache, or refusal), and add an eval case that injects a 429 and scores the fallback output.
